title: Inside the Pool of Gibeon: 3D Model Reconstruction and Some Observations About Finds
author: Maria Tamburrini
publisher: OSF preprint (Sapienza University of Rome, Italian Institute of Oriental Studies)
allowedUseNotes: Preprint/conference paper by a named PhD researcher. Project stores its own summary only; no reproduction of the 3D model, photographs, or figures.
summary: A PhD-research-based re-examination of Pritchard's original excavation records and finds from the cylindrical pool at Gibeon (el-Jib), combining a 3D model reconstruction of the pool structure with a reassessment of the stratigraphy of its earthen fill. Tamburrini's account dates the pool's construction to the 10th century BCE, and identifies a separate, later group of fragmentary artifacts (8th-6th century BCE) recovered from the same fill, which she reads as suggesting a more complex depositional history than a single accumulation event rather than as evidence the pool itself is a later construction.
confidenceNotes: TO VERIFY: this is a preprint (OSF/SocArXiv-style, DOI 10.31235/osf.io/5ajpc), not confirmed here as having appeared in a peer-reviewed journal — bibliographic details assembled from secondary search-result summaries (academia.edu/ResearchGate listing pages, author's own research-profile description), not from direct inspection of the paper's full text or Pritchard's original excavation volumes. The '10th century BCE' construction date is the most specific claim located for this open dating question (see claim-gibeon-pool-form's notes and docs/uncertainty-register.md #15): it does not by itself distinguish early vs. late 10th century, so it narrows but does not resolve whether the pool predates, is contemporary with, or postdates the early Iron IIA setting of 2 Samuel 2. No source located in this research pass argues for a 9th-8th century (postdating) construction specifically; the later artifact group (8th-6th c.) is read here as fill/use-phase material, not a construction date.
